blockers.title: The frozen Claude v20 review pin does not reproduce
evidence: The dispatch prompt and v21 appliesFindingsOf.claude2v20 both pin the frozen Claude v20 review at 0415c453293bc8a8063a429af9cf4329f98175e037bc04bd64c046534ba71393.
Python hashlib measured the named mode-0444 file at opening and closing as 343b0e598b1a5e068cb32e4a1d0da2463d40b4c2090ff4fbbf3d11b125ab297f. The required bytes are not present at the pinned path.

The observed replacement is COMPLETE REJECT and its raw blocker, SHOULD-FIX, and advisory identifiers happen to match the roster recorded in v21. Matching selected JSON fields does not establish byte custody or prove that unexamined fields equal the artifact whose digest v21 claims to fold.

The prompt expressly says predecessor-review replacement is not PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT and that pins must reproduce. The only exception is later append-only COORD movement with file 08 and the subject unmoved; it does not cover a frozen review.

appliesFindingsOf.idCollisionNote also says both that Claude v20 was in review at v21 authoring and is not pinned and that pin records retain the Claude pin, while basedOn.method and the actual claude2v20 member say it is pinned. That contradictory history cannot cure the missing bytes.
blockers.impact: The v21 succession claim cannot prove which Claude v20 review it folded. A replaced predecessor review can change evidence, required repairs, constraints, or conclusions without changing the small roster copied into appliesFindingsOf, so the independent-review chain is not reproducible.
blockers.requiredRepair: Do not rewrite or chmod the frozen file or v21. Establish the authentic frozen Claude v20 bytes and issue a new successor that pins their reproducing digest, or, if 343b0e59... is independently established as the authentic frozen artifact, issue a new successor that explicitly records the custody event and pins that exact immutable file. Remove the contradictory not-pinned/pinned history. Silent repinning or predecessor replacement is not a repair.

blockers.title: The Linux package-db operation authenticates package metadata but not the object or running kernel being admitted
evidence: For a file-backed event, owningPackageLookup runs rpm -qf or dpkg-query -S on a path. Those operations select an ownership record; no v21 step hashes the bytes of the opened resolved object, verifies those bytes against an installed-file manifest, or compares them with the payload represented by authenticityCore.payload.digest.

The rpm branch checks a package signature/status and reads SHA256HEADER from package metadata. The apt branch reads the installed name/version and a SHA256 from a trusted Packages index. Both branches can therefore produce the signed {name, version, digest} and result=success while the file at the owned path has been modified after installation.

A concrete counterexample satisfies every named join: install the signed package, alter an owned loader or framework file without changing the package database/index, resolve that altered file, let the ownership query return the original package, and retain the original package digest and successful metadata trust result. observedPlatformAttestation then equals the signed core even though the loaded bytes drifted.

The pathless branch has the same subject gap. runningKernelImagePath selects an on-disk file by an osrelease-derived filename and package ownership, but no rule proves that those disk bytes are the currently executing kernel or measures the executing kernel. Replacing the disk image after boot, or selecting a different same-release image, leaves the running kernel unattested.

NT-TCB-3 requires a declared object whose identity drifts to refuse. The package tuple is used as the object identity, but v21 never establishes that the actual object bytes are still the bytes represented by that tuple.
blockers.impact: A hostile modification of a mandatory Linux OS-ABI, loader, framework, or PLATFORM-ATTESTED libc object can be admitted under the unchanged signed package identity. This is a false allow, not merely a fail-closed coverage gap, and defeats the contract's central identity-drift property across required G22 cells.
blockers.requiredRepair: Bind the same opened object handle or immutable same-event byte source to the package verification and verify the actual object bytes against a signed package manifest or a precisely specified reconstruction from the authenticated package payload. Retain the evidence needed to prove that equality. For pathless OS ABI, define an observation that is cryptographically bound to the executing kernel/ABI subject rather than a same-release disk filename. Ownership metadata alone must never establish object authenticity.

shouldFix.title: The observedPlatformAttestation migration leaves live pathless rules on the removed bare observedAttestation field
evidence: v21 adds the closed producer-visible observedPlatformAttestation {authenticityCore, trustDecision} record to retainedEventSchema and the three later-event variants. That repairs the missing schema slot in the principal paths.

identitySerializations.observedAttestation still says producers emit the bare canonical authenticityCore only. A new note in the same object says producers MUST instead emit observedPlatformAttestation and that the bare core is incomplete. Both live producer instructions remain present.

Both subjectByScheme.binding rules still read observedAttestation.scheme/payload, and pathlessClasses.pathlessObservation.binding still joins observedAttestation authenticityCore. The PATHLESS laterEventVariant no longer has an observedAttestation field; it has observedPlatformAttestation.authenticityCore.

The new evidenceJoin and volumeConstraint join use the new path, while these retained rules use the old path. One implementation can treat the old name as an informal alias; another can enforce the closed later-event schema and reject it as absent.
shouldFix.impact: The trust result is representable, but mandatory pathless OS-ABI evidence still has two incompatible live field paths and opposite producer directions. This can cause deterministic valid evidence to be rejected or a bare, incomplete core to be emitted. The dominant new closed record prevents treating this residual as the original blocker, but it must be removed before acceptance.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace every live subjectByScheme and pathlessClasses reference with observedPlatformAttestation.authenticityCore, and change the legacy observedAttestation producersEmit rule to say it is only the nested core serialization and is never emitted as the complete event record. Keep the historical honesty ledger unchanged.

shouldFix.title: The named platform operation still contains undefined and cross-branch file inputs
evidence: linuxPackageDb.owningPackageLookup.fileBackedPath is defined as the canonical path of resolvedObjectIdentity. The live resolver rules say resolvedObjectIdentity is an authenticity identity and expressly forbid projecting a path from it. EXTERNAL-ORIGIN has resolverObservation.canonicalPath, but the lookup does not name it; INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME retains no equivalent same-event object path.

The global fileBackedBinding applies to loader, framework, libc, and every non-pathless PLATFORM-ATTESTED event and says to bind via owningPackageLookup.fileBackedPath. owningPackageLookup exists only under linuxPackageDb, so the same rule points macos/codesign events at a Linux-only operation despite macosCodesign already naming a different resolved-object guest input.

The rpm checksig argument remains the unresolved alternative <NEVRA-or-installed-package>, while the owner query claims one NEVRA and no rule selects one of the two spellings. The interface is explicitly unpinned across rpm majors, and success depends on a stdout token without a locale or byte normalization.

authenticityCore defines digest as sha-256 of one canonical package byte sequence, but the rpm branch obtains only the stored SHA256HEADER text and asserts that the rpmdb associates a payload with it; it neither names the bytes nor runs the required sha-256 operation. The apt branch similarly consumes an index field without a retained index/Release identity. These are not one closed, reproducible byte-collection algorithm.

runningKernelImagePath uses an or-choice between /boot/vmlinuz-* and /lib/modules/*/vmlinuz and a release-suffix condition without defining candidate enumeration, symlink/root anchoring, or how the suffix applies to the latter basename. Cardinality refusal does not make different enumerations equivalent.
shouldFix.impact: Even after the false-allow defect in PTCB-V21-B2 is repaired, two implementations can select different paths, command arguments, package bytes, or OS branches and produce different qualification outcomes for one profile. Some mandatory macOS and INSTALL-ROOT events have no executable interpretation of the stated binding.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define branch-specific file-backed bindings: the exact same SecCode guest/object handle for macOS, resolverObservation.canonicalPath and association token for EXTERNAL Linux events, and a newly retained same-event opened path/handle for INSTALL-ROOT Linux events. Replace every or-choice with one grammar, pin command/output normalization or define an API-independent algorithm, and specify exact package bytes plus their computed digest and retained trust/index identity.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 2 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. The frozen Claude v20 pin does not reproduce, and the Linux package-db flow can authenticate unchanged package metadata while admitting modified object or mismatched running-kernel bytes. The observed-attestation migration and file-input operation also retain live contradictions. The companion and observedAt repairs pass. DR-126 remains OPEN; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, G22 qualification, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
